title: Privacy-Aware Diabetic Retinopathy Classification Using Federated Learning an...

name: Title 1
text: Privacy-Aware Diabetic Retinopathy Classification Using Federated Learning and Explainable Deep Learning

name: Subtitle 2
text:
Presented by:
Lingeshwar G
Reg. No: 22MIS0558

name: TextBox 6
text:
Under the Guidance of:
Dr. Asha N
Associate Professor Grade 1

name: Content Placeholder 2
text:
Diabetic retinopathy is a diabetes-related eye disease affecting the retina.
It can progress from mild abnormalities to severe vision loss.
Retinal fundus images can be analyzed using deep learning.
Deep learning can automatically learn visual patterns associated with different DR stages.
However, centralized medical-image training creates privacy and data-sharing concerns.
EdgeRetina combines:
Deep Learning
Federated Learning
Privacy-Inspired Update Processing
Explainable AI

name: Content Placeholder 2
text:
Traditional centralized deep learning requires medical images from different sources to be collected at a central location.
Major Challenges
Privacy concerns associated with medical images
Data-sharing restrictions between institutions
Class imbalance in the APTOS dataset
Variations in retinal image quality
Difficulty in interpreting deep-learning predictions
Centralized training is not suitable for privacy-sensitive healthcare environments

name: lit_body_0
text: Fundus-image studies show that automated DR analysis is feasible. Strong results often use large, centrally collected datasets.

name: lit_body_1
text: FedAvg gives institutions a way to train on local data. Client differences and communication remain practical challenges.

name: lit_body_2
text: Updates can reveal information. Clipping and noise can reduce exposure, while formal differential privacy also needs calibrated accounting.

name: lit_body_3
text: Grad-CAM highlights image regions related to a class score. Its heatmap is coarse and does not segment lesions.

Explain that these are the report’s synthesis of prior studies, not results from EdgeRetina. Deep learning papers establish task feasibility; FL supports data locality but brings client and communication issues; formal DP needs an accountant; Grad-CAM is a coarse visual explanation. Sources: final report §§2.3–2.4, printed pp. 8–10. Key studies: Gulshan et al. (2016), Ting et al. (2017), McMahan et al. (2017), Rieke et al. (2020), Sheller et al. (2020), Abadi et al. (2016), Dwork and Roth (2014), Zhu et al. (2019), Selvaraju et al. (2017).

name: gap_statement
text: One runnable application connects five-grade classification, simulated federation, update processing and visual explanation.

name: gap_body_a
text:
APTOS validation and preprocessing
Two transfer-learning backbones
Four simulated clients with FedAvg
Clipping and Gaussian-noise processing
Flask interface, prediction history and Grad-CAM

name: gap_body_b
text:
A prototype, not a clinical device
Four clients run as software simulations
No formal (ε, δ) privacy guarantee
Results need stronger minority-grade recall
External and multi-site validation remain future work

The report positions EdgeRetina as a student-scale integration prototype. It does not claim state-of-the-art performance, formal privacy protection or clinical validation. Source: final report §2.5, printed p. 11, plus project README and current application modules.

text: Held-out test set: 550 images  |  higher is better

name: central_note
text: Macro-F1 gives each of the five grades equal weight.

These centralized values come from the report’s held-out 550-image test set. EfficientNetB0 has the best accuracy (71.1%); MobileNetV3Small has slightly better macro-F1 (42.0% vs 40.9%). Accuracy and macro-F1 differ because class performance is uneven. Source: final report, Chapter 9, Table 9.3 and §9.11, printed pp. 61–66; reports/experiments/mobilenetv3small.json and efficientnetb0.json.

name: fl_summary
text: 4 simulated clients  |  5 completed rounds  |  550 held-out images

name: fl_caveat
text: Later saved dashboard run. Its result is separate from the report’s centralized model comparison.

The project now contains reports/federated/evaluation.json for run 68688c55a1864640ab728b6f2032341c: MobileNetV3Small, five completed rounds, 550 held-out test images, accuracy 67.1%, macro-F1 40.1% and QWK 0.687. The report’s original results chapter stated that FL test metrics were unavailable when it was written. Present this as a later saved dashboard evaluation, not as a controlled comparison against the centralized runs. Project files: reports/federated/evaluation.json and reports/federated/rounds.json.

name: class_intro
text: The held-out set is uneven. The saved federated checkpoint missed all 29 Severe DR cases.

name: class_note
text: Accuracy can hide weak performance on less common grades. Macro-F1 and per-class recall show where the model needs work.

The held-out federated evaluation includes 271 No DR, 56 Mild, 150 Moderate, 29 Severe and 44 Proliferative cases. In the saved five-round checkpoint, severe DR recall is 0.0% (0 of 29), while No DR recall is 95.6%. This is the key caution behind reporting macro-F1 and per-class results alongside accuracy. These metrics describe this saved run only. Source: reports/federated/evaluation.json; report §9.9 and §9.11.

name: dp_step_3
text:
ADD GAUSSIAN NOISE
Δprocessed = Δclip + η
η ~ N(0, σ²I)

name: dp_step_4
text:
FEDAVG INPUT
Aggregate processed updates
Images stay in local splits

name: dp_caveat
text: Prototype illustration only. No privacy accountant or formal (ε, δ) guarantee is implemented.

PowerPoint animation: click once to reveal each step in order. This example uses an illustrative two-number update, not a real neural-network weight tensor. Start with Δ=[3,4], whose L2 norm is 5. With clip bound C=1, the scale is 1/5, producing Δclip=[0.6,0.8]. Then the implementation adds a zero-mean Gaussian value to each parameter. The code sets per-parameter noise scale to C × noise multiplier / sqrt(M), with multiplier 0.10 and M the number of model parameters. Processed client updates then enter sample-weighted FedAvg. This is privacy-inspired processing, not a formal differential-privacy guarantee: there is no accountant, (ε,δ) budget, secure aggregation or encryption. Source: backend/app/federated/differential_privacy.py, backend/app/federated/fedavg.py, final report §§6.5.1–6.5.4, printed pp. 36–38.

name: Content Placeholder 2
text:
Current Limitations
The federated learning environment uses simulated clients, not real hospitals.
The dataset is relatively limited and class-imbalanced.
Model performance varies across DR classes.
The current privacy mechanism does not provide a formally verified differential privacy guarantee.
No complete privacy accountant or explicit \((\epsilon,\delta)\) analysis is implemented.
Grad-CAM provides visual explanations but does not perform exact lesion segmentation.

name: Content Placeholder 2
text:
EdgeRetina combines deep learning, federated learning, privacy-inspired update processing, and explainable AI.
APTOS 2019 is used for five-class diabetic retinopathy classification.
MobileNetV3Small and EfficientNetB0 were implemented and evaluated.
EfficientNetB0 achieved 71.1% test accuracy.
MobileNetV3Small achieved 42.0% macro-F1.
Four simulated clients demonstrate the federated learning workflow.
FedAvg is used to generate the global model.
Update clipping and Gaussian noise are applied before aggregation.
Grad-CAM provides visual explanations.
Flask and SQLite provide the application and prediction-history functionality.
The final system is a research prototype for privacy-aware and explainable DR classification.
